subject.title: [Bug]: Subagents can appear completed before the underlying delegated work is actually finished

question: Should child-owned background exec/process work block subagent completion, or should it remain a separate active-work signal after the subagent agent-run completes?
rationale: Both behaviors are plausible from current code: blocking fixes false completion but can hang intentionally detached work, while separate surfacing preserves non-blocking semantics but requires clearer status and UX contracts.

options.title: Separate Active Work
options.body: Keep subagent completion tied to the child agent-run outcome and surface background exec/process liveness explicitly in task and session status views.

options.title: Block Completion On Owned Processes
options.body: Treat owned background processes as completion-required work with bounded timeout, cancellation, cleanup, and regression tests before subagent finalization.

options.title: Narrow To Delivery Fixes
options.body: Close this lifecycle direction in favor of narrower delivery and task-ledger issues, accepting that background processes are intentionally detached from subagent completion.

recommendation.title: Separate Active Work
recommendation.body: Keep subagent completion tied to the child agent-run outcome and surface background exec/process liveness explicitly in task and session status views.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent subagent task-owner reconciliation work is closest to the remaining completion-vs-task-state decision surface.
